headline_marked: Jamaat Ameer: [[BNP trying to establish one-party rule]] in Bangladesh
headline: Jamaat Ameer: BNP trying to establish one-party rule in Bangladesh
summary: Dr Shafiqur Rahman alleges the government is installing loyalists in key posts and ignoring the verdict of the referendum to consolidate power.
details: Bangladesh Jamaat-e-Islami Ameer Dr Shafiqur Rahman has alleged that the ruling BNP is attempting to establish one-party rule in the country, warning that the public will not accept such a system.

Speaking at a party conference in Narayanganj, the Jamaat chief cited the appointment of party loyalists as administrators in district councils and the appointment of the central bank governor as evidence of this trend.
He further alleged that the government is interfering in banks like Islami Bank and removing qualified university vice-chancellors to install party affiliates.
Dr Rahman referenced the historical precedent of BaKSAL, stating that Sheikh Mujibur Rahman's one-party system failed quickly and that the public would not tolerate a repeat of such a system.
The Ameer also criticized the BNP's stance on the referendum, claiming the party initially opposed it and later changed its position under public pressure.
He called on the government to respect the verdict of the referendum and stop the culture of belittling opposition parties in parliament, a practice he said was once used by the Awami League.
Regarding the national budget, he warned that while a large budget was announced, people need assurance that corruption and extortion will not continue.
He shared that local businesspeople in Narayanganj expressed fear and claimed that extortionists remain active and are preventing them from continue their business in peace.
caption:
Is history repeating itself? Jamaat-e-Islami Ameer warns that the BNP is attempting to establish one-party rule in Bangladesh.

Bangladesh Jamaat-e-Islami Ameer Dr Shafiqur Rahman has alleged that the ruling BNP is attempting to establish one-party rule in the country, warning that the public will not accept such a system.

Speaking at a party conference in Narayanganj, the Jamaat chief cited the appointment of party loyalists as administrators in district councils and the appointment of the central bank governor as evidence of this trend.

He further alleged that the government is interfering in banks like Islami Bank and removing qualified university vice-chancellors to install party affiliates.

Dr Rahman referenced the historical precedent of BaKSAL, stating that Sheikh Mujibur Rahman's one-party system failed quickly and that the public would not tolerate a repeat of such a system.

The Ameer also criticized the BNP's stance on the referendum, claiming the party initially opposed it and later changed its position under public pressure.

He called on the government to respect the verdict of the referendum and stop the culture of belittling opposition parties in parliament, a practice he said was once used by the Awami League.

Regarding the national budget, he warned that while a large budget was announced, people need assurance that corruption and extortion will not continue.

He shared that local businesspeople in Narayanganj expressed fear and claimed that extortionists remain active and are preventing them from continue their business in peace.

headline_marked: Measles outbreak: [[Death toll reaches 76]] in Sylhet Division
headline: Measles outbreak: Death toll reaches 76 in Sylhet Division
summary: Two more children have died with measles symptoms in the region, adding to a growing number of suspected cases and laboratory-confirmed infections.
details: Two more children have died with measles symptoms in Sylhet Division, according to Noore Alam Shamim, divisional director at Health Office Sylhet.
One of the deceased, 7-month-old baby Saihan, passed away while undergoing treatment at Shaheed Shamsuddin Ahmed Hospital.
In the 24 hours leading up to 8am on Friday, 261 patients with measles symptoms were receiving treatment at hospitals across the division.
During the same period, another 69 suspected measles patients were admitted to hospitals.
Since January 1, laboratory tests have confirmed measles infection in 327 people across the Sylhet Division.
The division has recorded 72 deaths among people with symptoms, with four of those being laboratory-confirmed measles cases.
